sources.entry: Tiny Tiny RSS - Web-based news feed (RSS/Atom) reader and aggregator. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 Docker/PHP

summary.one_liner: Tiny Tiny RSS (tt-rss) is a free, open-source, web-based reader and aggregator for RSS, Atom and other news feeds, now maintained as a community fork after the original project was retired.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes tt-rss as a web-based news feed (RSS/Atom/other) reader and aggregator. It is a self-described fork of the original tt-rss project, made from its 2025-10-03 state by a long-time contributor who intends to continue development. The README says Docker images for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 are built and published to Docker Hub and GitHub Container Registry, as drop-in replacements for the old images. Documentation has been recreated in a new repository, and plugins have been mirrored under a consistent tt-rss-plugin-* naming prefix. The README does not list specific features beyond feed reading and aggregation, and it points to an installation guide rather than giving setup steps inline. The minimum supported PHP version tracks Debian's current stable release.
use_cases: aggregate news feeds in one web interface
read Atom and RSS subscriptions in the browser
run a personal news aggregator with Docker
replace the retired original tt-rss deployment
how_to_run: Follow the installation guide referenced in the README (not included inline)
Optionally run the published Docker images: supahgreg/tt-rss and supahgreg/tt-rss-web-nginx on Docker Hub
Or use ghcr.io/tt-rss/tt-rss and ghcr.io/tt-rss/tt-rss-web-nginx from GitHub Container Registry
notable: Community fork continuing development after the original project was retired on 2025-11-01
Docker images for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 published via GitHub Actions
Minimum PHP version follows Debian's current stable release
Plugins mirrored with a consistent tt-rss-plugin-* repository prefix
caveats: The original tt-rss project was retired on 2025-11-01; this fork is the continuing line of development
The README gives no inline setup steps and refers to a separate installation guide
The README states that bugs sometimes slip through in the main branch
